prompt: I would like to outperform the S&P 500 in the next year. Can you propose 10 stocks I should buy?
reply:
# 10 Stocks to Research for Trying to Beat the S&P 500

No one can reliably pick stocks that will beat the S&P 500 over the next 12 months. In most years, most professional large-cap fund managers fail to beat it, and over 10–15 years roughly 85–90% fall behind (per S&P's SPIVA reports). One year is also a short window, so luck and market mood will drive much of your result.

My knowledge also ends in May 2026, so I don't know current prices, valuations or recent earnings. Treat the list below as ideas to research, not a buy list.

## A diversified watchlist with reasons and risks

| # | Stock | Why it could outperform | Main risk |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Microsoft (MSFT)** | Azure cloud and AI demand; sticky business software | High expectations already in the price; heavy AI spending |
| 2 | **Alphabet (GOOGL)** | Search, YouTube, Cloud, Gemini AI, Waymo; historically cheaper than other mega-caps | Antitrust rulings; AI chatbots taking search traffic |
| 3 | **Taiwan Semiconductor (TSM)** | Makes most of the world's advanced AI chips; not in the S&P 500, so it adds something different | China–Taiwan tensions; the chip cycle |
| 4 | **Broadcom (AVGO)** | Custom AI chips and networking; VMware software revenue | High valuation; reliance on a few large customers |
| 5 | **Eli Lilly (LLY)** | Leader in GLP-1 obesity and diabetes drugs; long growth runway | Drug pricing pressure; competition; high valuation |
| 6 | **JPMorgan Chase (JPM)** | Best-run large US bank; strong across its businesses | Recession or rising loan losses |
| 7 | **Visa (V)** | Earns a fee on card payments worldwide with high margins | Regulation; fees paid to merchants; new payment methods |
| 8 | **Berkshire Hathaway (BRK.B)** | Defensive anchor; large cash pile to buy in downturns | Adjusting after Buffett's handover to Greg Abel; tends to lag in strong bull markets |
| 9 | **GE Vernova (GEV)** | Gas turbines and power grid equipment for rising electricity demand from data centers | Stock has risen sharply; execution on large projects |
| 10 | **ASML (ASML)** | Only maker of the most advanced chip-making (EUV) machines; not in the S&P 500 | Export limits on sales to China; lumpy orders |

**About concentration:** about half of these names depend on AI spending (MSFT, GOOGL, TSM, AVGO, GEV, ASML). If that spending slows, several could fall together. To beat the index you have to own something *different* from it. Ten mega-cap tech stocks would mostly be a leveraged version of what the S&P already holds.

## How to approach this more sensibly

- **Core and satellite:** keep most of your money (e.g., 70–80%) in a low-cost S&P 500 index fund (VOO, SPY, IVV, or a UCITS version like CSPX if you're outside the US). Use the rest for your stock picks. You get a chance to beat the index without risking badly trailing it.
- **Equal-weight your picks** (about 2–3% each within the satellite) so one bad call doesn't sink you.
- **Check each one before buying:** current valuation (P/E versus its own history), the last two earnings reports, and what could break the investment case.
- **Set rules in advance:** when you'd sell, when you'd rebalance, and how you'll judge success. A fair test is the total return including dividends, compared with the S&P 500's total return.
- **Consider fund-based tilts** as another option, such as equal-weight S&P (RSP), quality (QUAL) or momentum (MTUM). They aren't guaranteed to win either, but they are diversified.
- **If you invest from outside the US,** check the withholding tax on US dividends. Also check US estate-tax exposure, since non-residents can owe it on large holdings of US stocks.

If you share your time horizon beyond one year, your risk tolerance, how much of your savings this is, and where you're investing from, I can adjust the list or the allocation. For a large amount of money, a licensed financial adviser is worth considering.
